followups.body:
<!-- stammbaum-followup:E02 -->

## Outcome and scope

Offer deliberate recovery of supported unsaved research drafts after reload or browser closure without automatic submission or disclosure across accounts. This is a post-parity enhancement requested during the alpha.15 gap review; #29 explicitly makes no promise that drafts survive browser closure. Existing in-session draft protection remains a parity obligation.

Reference: #29 (W05, FORM/KOLL; specification chapters 3 and 9, A15/A23) and docs/iteration-01.md. A15/A23 supply conflict/navigation regressions; they do not establish a cross-session persistence requirement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Specify the supported editors, storage location, consent/default behavior, bounded retention/size, schema version and account/tree/record namespace before implementation. Explain local-device privacy and storage limitations honestly.
- [ ] Before showing recovered research, reauthenticate through Nextcloud as needed and recheck current account, membership and all record/dependency permissions; switching users, removal/rejoin or recreated identities cannot expose old drafts.
- [ ] Present explicit Restore/Discard with current server revision and deliberate conflict comparison. Recovery never silently submits or overwrites research.
- [ ] Handle storage denied, quota exhausted, corrupted/unknown-version drafts and concurrent tabs without losing the current in-memory edit or claiming persistence succeeded.
- [ ] Define cleanup on successful save, explicit discard, expiry, logout/account change and authority loss. Do not persist credentials, upload bytes or signed download URLs in draft payloads.
- [ ] Use fictional fixtures and Playwright browser-context restarts to verify recovery, stale versions, offline/failure behavior, revoked access, user switching and keyboard operation in English/German. Verify navigation/recovery alone never changes genealogy or tree revisions.

## Native contracts and exclusions

Nextcloud remains the authority for identity and sessions. Coordinate supported draft payloads with record revisions and existing idempotent creates; define upgrade compatibility and safe rejection of obsolete drafts. No automatic merge, automatic save, cross-device synchronization, promise of recovery after storage clearing, or indefinite offline access to private genealogy.

Dependencies: #29, #11. Roadmap: #1. Deferred enhancement; excluded from parity milestone completion.
